title: The Partridge, the Monkey and the Elephant
text:
Near a great banyan tree in the Himalayan foothills lived three friends: a partridge, a monkey and an elephant. They often fell out, and none treated the others with respect. At last they decided that life would go better if they agreed to honor the eldest among them. But who was the eldest?

The elephant spoke first. When he was a young calf, he said, this banyan was only a bush, and as he walked over it, its top branches brushed his belly. The monkey said that when he was a baby, he sat on the ground and nibbled the shoots at the very top of the young tree. The partridge then explained that long ago there had been another great banyan elsewhere. He had eaten its fruit and dropped a seed here, and from that seed this very tree had grown.

So the partridge was the oldest. The monkey and the elephant honored him and followed his advice, and the three lived together in harmony from then on. In the Jataka, the Buddha tells this story to his monks when they fail to give their senior members proper lodging.
lesson: Groups argue less when they agree in advance on a fair rule for who decides. A clear, shared order of respect can settle disputes before they start.
people: A partridge, a monkey, an elephant
